primary_source_support.verified_fact: The WAL-reset corruption bug affects WAL-mode releases through 3.51.2 and is fixed in 3.51.3 and later; 3.53.4 is on the fixed side. Productive runtime identity still must be proven rather than inferred from a version string.

grf.hypothesis: The strengthened endpoint mapping checks could be interpreted as continuous SQLite mapping identity across a surrounding productive persistence operation.
grf.strongest_counter_reality: A same-PID process can leave the expected SQLite mapping, transiently add another SQLite mapping identity, and return to the exact original mapping before the next endpoint sample.
grf.falsifier: Perform a real Linux same-process mapping ABA cycle and compare mapping identity before, during, and after.

unusual_experiment.name: LIVE_SQLITE_MAPPING_TEMPORAL_ABA
unusual_experiment.method: Load the process system libsqlite3, snapshot /proc/self/maps, load a temporary copied libsqlite3.so.0 into the same PID, snapshot again, dlclose the temporary mapping, then snapshot once more.
limitations: The temporary object was a byte copy of the same local SQLite library, not an older or malicious SQLite build.
This demonstrates a temporal observability/ABA gap between samples, not a production exploit and not a failure of the attestor's explicitly narrow final-observation claim.
No Frank process, database, WAL, accepted Hostinger service, canonical state, or effect authority was touched.

collapse.claim: Equal SQLite mapping identities at two sampled endpoints prove that no different SQLite mapping existed between those endpoints.
The current live-process attestor is useful as a fail-closed point observation for one process generation.
collapse.reason: Its code and receipt already state the narrow scope and re-sample the mapping after receipt-tail metadata.

collapse.claim: The ABA observation alone justifies another attestor patch.
collapse.reason: No finite endpoint sampler proves continuous absence of transient remapping; changing point-sampling code would Goodhart the wrong proxy.

collapse.claim: F-V01-13 or Frank v0.1 is complete.
collapse.reason: Accepted productive Hostinger persistence/restart/rollback binding, semantic lineage and terminal acceptance evidence remain open.

architecture_delta.new_invariant: Do not promote a sampled SQLite mapping receipt into a claim of continuous productive persistence identity unless the productive operation itself is causally bound to the observed fixed runtime or an explicit continuous anti-remap threat-control is measured.
architecture_delta.rollback: No product code changed; remove only this research interpretation if a stronger accepted-host causal binding makes the temporal counterworld irrelevant under the canonical threat model.

next_falsifier.test: On the accepted Hostinger product service, exercise the exact Frank database/WAL persistence path across a controlled write/checkpoint plus restart, bind the executing Frank generation, database path, trust anchor, SQLite source/build/hash and actual mapped object, then run downgrade/library-swap and rollback controls. Record whether the canonical threat model requires continuous same-generation anti-remap protection or only trusted deployment/restart identity.
next_falsifier.success_condition: Productive persistence and restart evidence is causally bound to the accepted fixed SQLite object and all stale/downgraded/swapped/rollback controls fail closed.
next_falsifier.do_not_substitute: self-hosted CI, endpoint-only mapping receipt, version string, or synthetic process for accepted productive Hostinger persistence evidence
